parts.text: The Soil Food Web Foundation was established in October 2025
to carry forward the life's work of Dr. Elaine Ingham, the
pioneering scientist whose research transformed our
understanding of soil biology and its central role in food
production, ecosystem health, and planetary regeneration.

runs.text:
The Soil Food Web Foundation was established in October 2025 to carry
        forward the life's work of Dr. Elaine Ingham, the pioneering scientist
        whose research transformed our understanding of soil biology and its
        central role in food production, ecosystem health, and planetary
        regeneration.

parts.text: She passed away in February 2026, and the work she started
continues through the Foundation, the school that is a part of it,
and Soil Food Web practitioners in more than 132 countries, who
are helping to restore the world's soils.

parts.text: Soil carbon sequestration is widely recognized as a part
of the solution to climate change impacts. Plants pull
carbon from the air and invest much of it in the soil, where
it is built into microbial bodies, aggregates and complex
fungal networks. A biological approach to soil
fertilizer and irrigation needs and creates more nutritious
crops. Regenerating the world's soils using the Soil Food
Web Approach can improve atmospheric carbon levels.

runs.text:
Soil carbon
          sequestration is widely recognized as a part of the solution to
          climate change impacts. Plants pull carbon from the air and invest
          much of it in the soil, where it is built into microbial bodies,
          aggregates and complex fungal networks. A biological approach to soil
          management reduces equipment emissions, reduces fertilizer and
          irrigation needs and creates more nutritious crops. Regenerating the
          world's soils using the Soil Food Web Approach can improve atmospheric
          carbon levels. Be part of the soil-ution!

parts.text: We train people who help farmers to transition away from
using chemicals, to using biology. This results in
significant benefits to the farmer and to the environment,
as well as to the consumer. The method has been proven
effective on 6 continents and across all soil types, as
evidenced by our ever-increasing case study library.

parts.text: Though the projects run from backyard gardens to
expansive public parks, the same process is applicable. The
steps are the same at every scale: look at the biology under
a microscope, add what is missing to rebalance the
microbial content, then measure again to confirm microbial
counts are going in the expected directions.
